preamble: Direct vocalization of [l] to the mid back vowel [o]. It is the hallmark of Štokavian Serbo-Croatian: Proto-Slavic coda *l became o, creating a new syllable (pepeo 'ash', posao 'work', past participles in -ao/-io); the lateral reappears wherever a vowel follows (genitive pepela, posla). In English, the accents of Bristol and London (Cockney, Estuary English) vocalize final and syllabic /l/ to a back vocoid that is often [o]: Bristol bottle /ˈbɒto/, London girl [ɡɛo]. Elsewhere dark l usually vocalizes to [u] or [w], which reaches [o] only through further changes (e.g. French au > o).

examples.note: Genitive pepela keeps the lateral before a vowel.
Coda /l/ fully vocalized to /o/; Kajkavian and Torlakian dialects did not undergo the change.
Ijekavian dialectal bio; the name Beograd 'white city' contains the same form.
In the Bristol accent syllabic /l/ is vocalized to /o/; by hypercorrection some words in final /o/ gained an /l/, as in the city name Bristow > Bristol.
In London speech the vocalized /l/ varies [o ~ ʊ ~ ɯ] and also appears before a vowel (girl out [ɡɛo ˈæoʔ]); Estuary English bottle is [ˈbɒʔo].
